principle: Improve the existing browser game. Preserve playable scale, saved progress and the delivery route. Add tested interactions before enlarging the map.

cards.title: A connected investigation
cards.detail: Five stages: newsroom kit, Nia at Signal Plaza, security-yard evidence, quay report, publication. The original eight-paper route remains available.
cards.acceptance: Complete the investigation with ordinary input, reload its progress, and continue roaming after publication.

cards.title: Enter, drive, park and leave cars
cards.detail: Three enterable cars, steering, brake/reverse, a handbrake, fuel and condition. One moving taxi with simple signal/nearby-player stopping. Bikes and electric unicycle retained.
cards.acceptance: Drive from the neighborhood to the plaza and quay; exit into clear space. Collisions cannot pass through authored buildings.

cards.title: Fictional network interactions
cards.detail: Scan and select devices; hold to link at range with line of sight. Power feeds a gate; camera loops, traffic red, a speaker diversion and vehicle stop commands change simulation state.
cards.acceptance: No action without range and dwell; gate requires power; obstruction blocks the link. No external networks are accessed.

cards.title: A controllable remote drone
cards.detail: Fly, ascend/descend, scan and link over the checkpoint. Battery and range are bounded. Recall returns control to the stationary, vulnerable player body.
cards.acceptance: Extract evidence remotely without moving the body or secretly opening the gate.

cards.title: First stealth and alert model
cards.detail: Two patrols use range, forward sight and solid occlusion. Crouching lowers sight height; cover blocks detection. Trace rises and decays, and a nonlethal pulse disrupts patrols. This is not a complete six-star wanted system.
cards.acceptance: Cover and camera loops affect observation; breaking sight lets trace clear. Interception retries rather than closing the game.

cards.title: Small garage economy
cards.detail: In-game starter credits, one-time delivery/side-job rewards, service and a nitro upgrade. Traveled distance is recorded; it does not yet confer RPG bonuses.
cards.acceptance: Presence and funds required. No duplicate purchase or replayed reward. Purchases persist locally, with no real-money transactions.

cards.title: Three-route human playtest and navigation
cards.detail: Tune front gate, rear alley and drone approaches for readability and fun. Add selectable personal waypoints, better in-world directions and contextual controls.
cards.acceptance: Fresh players finish all three routes without developer instructions or unavoidable detection; each has a distinct reward/tradeoff.

cards.title: Third-person combat and real cover controls
cards.detail: Aim, nonlethal/lethal tool choices, enter/leave cover, peek and blind fire, reload, damage feedback and breakable authored props. Optional location-specific hits and vehicle/tire damage; no graphic detail required.
cards.acceptance: Controller, keyboard and touch all operate the same simulation. No shooting through cover. A complete mission remains solvable without combat.

cards.title: Better driving and responsive city traffic
cards.detail: Road graph, turning traffic, pedestrian crossings, actual collision avoidance, suspension/lean, wheel rotation and NPC reactions. Better motorcycle and bicycle handling, front-facing motorcycle attacks later with combat.
cards.acceptance: No taxi oscillation, invisible collision walls or trapped routes. Track frame time and draw budgets on real devices.

cards.title: Rooftops, vaulting and RC scout
cards.detail: Authored climb/vault ledges, fences, roof routes, multiple entry points, a ground RC scout and a small connected interior. Current hop over one low barrier is not full parkour.
cards.acceptance: Hand/foot contacts and head clearance agree with collision. Body, drone and RC routes use distinct obstacles; no teleports through roofs.

cards.title: Art and sound benchmark pass
cards.detail: Character-scale streets, denser original architecture, believable foliage and skyline, animation and richer materials. Original or explicitly licensed radio/music, satirical ads and talk segments; no copied franchise tracks/stations.
cards.acceptance: Compare actual playable screenshots and movement to the user's references, not concept images. Mute/pause and graphics recovery work; audit asset licenses.

cards.title: Six-tier pursuit and world response
cards.detail: Escalating patrol tactics, roadblocks, search areas, disguises and high-tier response. A wanted meter must emerge from simulated witnesses and responders, not spawn unavoidable punishment.
cards.acceptance: Every tier has readable escalation/de-escalation and escapable routes; maintain frame budget and nonviolent objectives.

cards.title: Service jobs and open-world discoveries
cards.detail: Taxi, paramedic, firefighter and vigilante job frameworks, hidden packages, unique stunt jumps, optional timed challenges, conversations and collectible trails.
cards.acceptance: Each activity has a playable loop, failure/retry, reward, save behavior and anti-farming rules. No quest progression dead ends.

cards.title: Clothes, garages and light RPG growth
cards.detail: Clothing, hair and tattoos; paint, rims, hydraulics, engine handling and nitro tuning. Stamina from running, strength training and driving/weapon proficiency with explicit bounded effects.
cards.acceptance: Changes are visible and saved, costs transparent, bonuses measurable and reversible. Appearance choices are never fabricated account entitlements.

cards.title: Enterable places and property businesses
cards.detail: Malls, hotels, mansions, workshops and studios; buy businesses such as a taxi company or fictional print shop. Active management missions and bounded income replace an idle cash exploit.
cards.acceptance: Interiors stream without wiping the exterior state; ownership, time and income reconcile safely across save/reload.

cards.title: Factions, crews and territory
cards.detail: Recruit allies; relationships, gang conflicts, corrupt officials, criminal contacts, rival crews and district control. James and Open Signal can take principled, compromising or criminal paths in original stories.
cards.acceptance: Choice affects missions, allies and world response. Nonviolent or solo alternatives remain viable; territorial saves cannot deadlock progression.

cards.title: Three larger regions, then a state-scale world
cards.detail: Expand from neighborhood/plaza/quay to connected islands, downtown, countryside, deserts and mountains. These are future regions, not unlocked content already hidden in the current map.
cards.acceptance: Implement chunk streaming, LOD, road/navigation graph and persistent world state before promising a huge map. Every region needs authored activities, not empty size.

cards.title: Water and heavy transport
cards.detail: Swimming, diving, boats, bicycles, trains, semitrailers and harvesters with distinct controls and activities.
cards.acceptance: Buoyancy, underwater camera, train graph and trailer joints use tested physics; safe recovery from capsizing or leaving the vehicle.

cards.title: Flying, parachutes and jetpack
cards.detail: Aircraft, airborne missions, parachutes and a fictional jetpack, with separate flight spaces and landing routes.
cards.acceptance: World streaming handles altitude/speed, controls work on supported devices, and every vehicle has bounded fuel and recovery behavior.

cards.title: World and mission authoring tools
cards.detail: A connected-road editor, object palette, mission graph, alternative-route validators, versioned scene documents and portable exports. Preserve the separate side-scroller Workshop; do not pretend it already edits this city.
cards.acceptance: Undo/redo, save/export/import and playtest use the same authoritative world document; validate reachability and references.

cards.title: Cloud saves, accounts and multiplayer
cards.detail: Supabase-backed authentication and versioned saves; later server-authoritative shared missions, traffic/physics ownership and co-op. No backend was provisioned in v0.3.0.
cards.acceptance: Owner-only policies, offline/merge recovery, rate limits, secret separation, security tests and low-latency authority model before public multiplayer.

cards.title: Membership purchases and coupon access
cards.detail: Optional paid memberships and coupon-created entitlements after the account system is secure. No live payment endpoints, prices, coupons or real charges are created by this milestone.
cards.acceptance: Agree products and terms first; test-mode checkout, server-verified webhook signatures, idempotent grants, abuse limits, cancellation/refund handling and explicit production approval.

cards.title: Controller, accessibility and device stability
cards.detail: Gamepad remapping, touch ergonomics, reduced motion, readable HUD, recovery diagnostics and real desktop/phone coverage. Retain no automatic quit on mission completion.
cards.acceptance: Human playtests on real devices, sustained-memory/frame-time budgets, blocked-storage tests and WebGL recovery with active city/drone state.
